symbols.name: \mathcal X
symbols.def: \(\mathcal X=(\mathcal X_V:V\in\mathcal V)\) fixes every observed alphabet in every domain.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The common latent-projection graph.

symbols.name: \mathcal D(G)
symbols.def: The maximal bidirected-connected components of \(G\).

symbols.name: \mathcal S
symbols.def: The target and source environment labels.

symbols.name: \star
symbols.def: The environment in which target counterfactuals are evaluated.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: A generic source or target environment.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: A generic district of the common graph.

symbols.name: T_{\mathrm{tr}}
symbols.def: The treatment vertex in the complete binary check.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The outcome vertex in the complete binary check.

symbols.name: Z

symbols.name: \Delta_s
symbols.def: The vertices whose mechanisms may differ between domain \(s\) and domain \(\star\).

symbols.name: \mathbf M
symbols.def: A family of finite recursive SCMs sharing \(G\) and the declared observed alphabets.

symbols.name: P^s
symbols.space: probability laws on the declared finite multiworld response space

symbols.name: \mathfrak M
symbols.def: The class defined in \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_s
symbols.space: finite sets of observational, interventional, and declared partial-copy regimes
symbols.def: The population laws supplied from domain \(s\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A generic declared regime in domain \(s\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: A generic atom measured under regime \(a\).

symbols.name: P_a^s
symbols.space: probability simplices on the random vector declared by \(a\)
symbols.def: The exact law supplied for descriptor \(a\) in domain \(s\).

symbols.name: \mathcal P
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P=\{P_a^s:s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}
symbols.space: finite sets of declared partial-copy regimes
symbols.def: The deployable actions in the target structural-causal bandit.

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.def: A generic deployable partial-copy regime.

symbols.name: \sigma
symbols.def: A comparator partial-copy regime.

symbols.name: E
symbols.space: events in the finite multiworld response space induced by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\)
symbols.def: The evidence event shared by the arm values under comparison.

symbols.name: B_\rho
symbols.space: events in the finite multiworld response space induced by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\)
symbols.def: The favorable reward event under arm \(\rho\).

symbols.name: Q_\rho^\star
symbols.def: \(Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)\) whenever \(P_{M^\star}(E)>0\).

symbols.name: \Omega_D
symbols.def: The deterministic response maps for \(D\) at every parent configuration visited by the targets and typed menus.

symbols.name: q_D^s
symbols.def: The probability vector on deterministic district profiles induced by \(M^s\).

symbols.name: W_a
symbols.def: The observed coordinates carried by the supplied law \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\).

symbols.name: H_{s,a,D}
symbols.def: The contexts for which fixing and marginalization of \(P_a^s\) expose a certified district kernel for \(D\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: A conditioning or fixing context certified as available from the supplied law.

symbols.name: C_{s,a,D}
symbols.def: The district cells returned by a successful extraction from descriptor \(a\) at district \(D\).

symbols.name: K_{s,a,D}
symbols.def: The kernel returned only by a certified successful extraction of \(P_a^s\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}
symbols.def: The partial fixing-and-marginalization map equipped with a certificate for every quotient it performs.

symbols.name: r_{s,a,D,h,c}
symbols.def: The indicator that a district response profile produces extracted cell \(c\) at certified context \(h\) under regime \(a\).

symbols.name: A_D
symbols.def: The normalization row followed by every transport-admissible source-labelled incidence row extractable for district \(D\).

symbols.name: m_D
symbols.def: The vector containing one followed by the exact supplied cell probabilities in the row order of \(A_D\).

symbols.name: \mathcal K_D(m_D)
symbols.def: The nonnegative response laws satisfying all stacked menu equalities.

symbols.name: Z_D(m_D)
symbols.def: The profiles assigned probability zero by every law in \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).

symbols.name: e_\omega
symbols.def: The unit coordinate row at \(\omega\in\Omega_D\).

symbols.name: b_D
symbols.def: The incidence row for a target district cell after counterfactual reduction.

symbols.name: n_{\rho,D}
symbols.def: The target district row for \(B_\rho\cap E\).

symbols.name: n_{\sigma,D}
symbols.def: The target district row obtained from \(B_\rho\cap E\) by substituting \(\sigma\) for the arm index.

symbols.name: d_D
symbols.def: The target district row for \(E\).

symbols.name: g_{\rho,\sigma,D}
symbols.def: \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\).

symbols.name: Q_\rho(q)
symbols.def: \(Q_\rho(q)=n_{\rho,D}q/(d_Dq)\) whenever \(d_Dq>0\).

symbols.name: Q_\sigma(q)
symbols.def: \(Q_\sigma(q)=n_{\sigma,D}q/(d_Dq)\) whenever \(d_Dq>0\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
symbols.def: The least numerator advantage of arm \(\sigma\) over arm \(\rho\) on the compatible face.

symbols.name: \overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
symbols.def: The greatest numerator advantage of arm \(\sigma\) over arm \(\rho\) on the compatible face.

symbols.name: \eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}
symbols.space: real vectors indexed by the rows of \(A_D\)
symbols.def: A dual weighting of supplied menu equalities certifying a lower bound on \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q\).

symbols.name: r_D^\dagger
symbols.def: The row induced by one additional realizable source-labelled partial-copy menu cell.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: The population value attached to \(r_D^\dagger\).

symbols.name: q(p)
symbols.def: \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\) for \(0\le p\le1/2\) in the complete binary check.

symbols.name: I_D
symbols.def: The attainable values of \(r_D^\dagger q\) over \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
symbols.def: The sharp gap margin after imposing the additional menu equality \(r_D^\dagger q=p\).

symbols.name: \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+
symbols.def: The candidate-cell values for which the parametric margin is strictly positive.

symbols.name: \mathcal U
symbols.def: The offline experiments available for acquiring source-labelled Layer-3 regime blocks.

symbols.name: e
symbols.def: A generic realizable offline regime-block acquisition.

symbols.name: e^\dagger
symbols.def: The sole unit-cost regime block in the complete binary acquisition check.

symbols.name: R_e
symbols.def: The dependent collection of menu rows jointly revealed by experiment \(e\).

symbols.name: p_e
symbols.def: The jointly realized cell probabilities paired with \(R_e\).

symbols.name: c_e
symbols.def: The positive acquisition cost of experiment \(e\).

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: A subset of regime blocks acquired ex post.

symbols.name: T_{\mathrm{exp}}
symbols.def: A selected experiment set containing \(S\) in the submodularity comparison.

symbols.name: \mathcal K_S
symbols.def: The laws on the base compatible face satisfying every acquired block equality.

symbols.name: \operatorname{PO}(S)
symbols.def: The arms maximizing their value at some law in \(\mathcal K_S\).

symbols.name: \mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U)\).

symbols.name: f(S)
symbols.def: \(f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C(\mathcal P)
symbols.def: The families in \(\mathfrak M\) inducing every supplied law in \(\mathcal P\).

symbols.name: \mathscr R(\mathcal P)
symbols.def: The algebra generated by typed-menu cells with division only by certified nonzero quantities.

symbols.name: F_B
symbols.def: A successful recursion output for the target numerator.

symbols.name: F_E
symbols.def: A successful recursion output for the evidence probability.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Atom}
symbols.def: Atoms with explicit domain labels, finite intervention or partial-copy terms, variables, and values; the normalization checker maps them to canonical unnested atoms.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Event}
symbols.def: Finite counterfactual events compiled by the normalization checker to a canonical disjoint normal form, including contradiction and sure-event forms.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Goal}
symbols.space: finite inductive syntax with checked derivations
symbols.def: Nodes are raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved finite-sum, unresolved finite-product, or resolved-expression nodes.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Expr}
symbols.def: Expressions generated by typed-menu cells, finite sums, products, and quotients carrying nonzero certificates.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Config}
symbols.space: finite well-typed acyclic work DAGs with two distinguished roots and traces
symbols.def: A configuration is a phase-indexed work DAG for the numerator and denominator, together with canonical node identifiers, two roots, and the checked transition trace.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Result}
symbols.def: The terminals are \(\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)\), \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\), and \(\operatorname{FAIL}(t)\), with derivation \(\delta\), zero certificate \(z\), and failure trace \(t\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}
symbols.def: For a nonterminal configuration, \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\), counting respectively raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved-sum, unresolved-product nodes, and one terminalization flag; every terminal has rank \((0,\ldots,0)\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}
symbols.def: The class of finite semi-Markovian district-closed source-labelled instances accepted by the DCTFTR grammar.

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}
symbols.type: observational and hard-interventional CTFTR instance class
symbols.def: The CTFTR subgrammar having only observational and hard-interventional supplied laws.

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}
symbols.def: The one-causal-specification Layer-3 input setting represented by \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}
symbols.def: The binary \(T\to Y\) plus isolated \(Z\) target--source instance specified in \(\mathrm{def:binary\text{-}check}\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)
symbols.space: finite unions of products of probability simplices and one-hot structural-table sets
symbols.def: The Zhang--Tian--Bareinboim finite canonical parameterization restricted to recursive SCMs compatible with \(G\) on the declared observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

symbols.name: \theta
symbols.def: A tuple of finite exogenous probability vectors and one-hot structural tables, one canonical block per domain.

symbols.name: C
symbols.space: events in the finite multiworld response space induced by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\)
symbols.def: A generic supplied or target counterfactual cell evaluated by recursive canonical-SCM substitution.

symbols.name: \Phi_C^s(\theta)
symbols.space: real multivariate polynomials on the canonical parameter space
symbols.def: The probability of cell \(C\) obtained by finite recursive evaluation in domain \(s\) and summation over canonical exogenous states.

symbols.name: \Theta(\mathcal P)
symbols.space: compact finite-dimensional semialgebraic subsets of \(\prod_{s\in\mathcal S}\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\)
symbols.def: The canonical parameter tuples satisfying graph, factorization, unchanged-district response-law, and every complete supplied-menu cell equality.

symbols.name: \mathcal F
symbols.space: finite sets of target-domain counterfactual cells
symbols.def: A finite collection used to compare joint target-cell ranges of the SCM and canonical compatibility fibers.

symbols.name: T
symbols.space: events in the finite multiworld response space induced by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\)
symbols.def: The target cell whose exact global canonical lower and upper probabilities are optimized.

symbols.name: L_T(\mathcal P)
symbols.type: sharp global canonical lower target-cell bound
symbols.def: The minimum of \(\Phi_T^\star\) over \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\).

symbols.name: U_T(\mathcal P)
symbols.type: sharp global canonical upper target-cell bound
symbols.def: The maximum of \(\Phi_T^\star\) over \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\).

symbols.name: e_-
symbols.def: The minimum of \(\Phi_E^\star\) over \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\).

symbols.name: e_+
symbols.def: The maximum of \(\Phi_E^\star\) over \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)=\Phi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)-\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).

novel.justification: A shared laboratory pipeline, record-linkage platform, or policy module can preserve the entire latent response block for a confounded district across sites. This is deliberately stronger than ordinary vertex-level selection-diagram invariance because Layer-3 laws depend on cross-world coupling inside the district.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).

novel.justification: Site changes often act on an entire confounded measurement or policy block. Whole-district selection permits arbitrary changes inside that block while ruling out an unsupported splice of cross-world dependence across only part of it.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

definitions.name: District-closed finite transport class
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

definitions.name: Typed-menu compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]

definitions.name: Canonical district response profile
definitions.construction: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).

definitions.name: Certified typed extraction judgment
definitions.construction: For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\), write \[\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\] exactly when consistency, unnesting, ancestor restriction, fixing, and marginalization define a kernel \(K_{s,a,D}:H_{s,a,D}\to\Delta(C_{s,a,D})\) and \(\kappa\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) certifies every context, marginal, and nonzero divisor used. An undefined fixing, unavailable context, or uncertified quotient has no successful judgment.

definitions.name: Context-indexed extracted-cell incidence row
definitions.construction: \[r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\text{ produces extracted cell }c\text{ at context }h\text{ under regime }a\},\qquad\omega_D\in\Omega_D.\]

definitions.name: Source-labelled stacked district system
definitions.construction: For every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\). Only then retain, for every available \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), the row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\). Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the retained rows as \(A_D\), and stack one and the retained kernel cells as \(m_D\). Failed extraction creates no row.

definitions.name: Face-aware district response polytope
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},\qquad Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.\]

definitions.name: Common-evidence arm row system
definitions.construction: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).

definitions.name: Sharp transported dominance margin
definitions.construction: \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\min_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q,\qquad \overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q.\]

definitions.name: Menu-dual dominance certificate
definitions.construction: A certificate at level \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) satisfying \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) coordinatewise and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\ge\gamma\).

definitions.name: One-cell Layer-3 sign-regime frontier
definitions.construction: \[I_D=\{r_D^\dagger q:q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\},\qquad\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=\min_{\substack{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\\ r_D^\dagger q=p}}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q,\qquad\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=\{p\in I_D:\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)>0\}.\]

definitions.name: Finite ex-post regime-block acquisition problem
definitions.construction: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]

definitions.name: Complete binary acquisition and strictness instance
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so the invariant district is \(D=\{Y\}\). Set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\), \(B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_0\ne Y_1\}\), \(B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_1=1\}\), and \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\). Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). The sole block has \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), \(R_{e^\dagger}=r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1)\), and reveals the genuine Layer-3 source cell \(p_{e^\dagger}=p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=3/8\). Also set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).

definitions.name: Allowed rational functional
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) is the typed expression-and-certificate algebra generated from menu cells by finite sums, differences, products, marginalization sums, and quotients carrying a proof that the divisor is nonzero on the relevant compatibility fiber.

definitions.name: DCTFTR syntax, configurations, and terminals
definitions.construction:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, regimes, districts, assignments, and generated DAG-node identifiers. The event grammar is \[\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]\,V_{\alpha}=v,\qquad \mathsf{Event}::=	op\mid ot\mid\mathsf{Atom}\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},\] where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term and canonical normalized events are disjoint normal forms of unnested atoms. Identified expressions have grammar \[\mathsf{Expr}::=\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,u)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,G,
u_G),\] where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(
u_G\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate. The phase-indexed node grammar is exactly \[\mathsf{Goal}::=\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\mid\operatorname{Normed}(	au,e,
u)\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e,\alpha)\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),\] with \(	au\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\). A configuration is a finite well-typed acyclic work DAG of these nodes, its numerator and denominator roots, and a checked trace. For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), node denotation is defined recursively: the first three event phases denote their target event probability; \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\) and \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\) denote \(bq_D^\star(\mathbf M)\); \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta)\) denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\); and sum and product nodes denote the corresponding finite sum and product of child denotations. Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root values. Checked derivations are finite syntax trees: normalization derivations use only consistency, unnesting, contradiction, Boolean normalization, and finite disjoint-additivity constructors; ancestor derivations enumerate summed assignments; district-split derivations enumerate the districts of \(G[H]\) and use finite marginalization and semi-Markovian district factorization; extraction derivations record each fixing, marginalization, context lookup, and certified quotient; face certificates are exact rational LP or Farkas certificates; and zero, nonzero, or strict-positivity certificates are checked by exact rational ring normalization together with Farkas certificates for linear face constraints or displayed sum-of-squares preordering identities for the finite response-law constraints. Thus no certificate constructor consists merely of the semantic equality or inequality being certified. The terminals are \[\mathsf{Result}::=\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t),\] where a conditioning derivation \(\delta\) records the numerator derivation, denominator derivation, and positivity certificate. Failure constructors include \(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t)\), \(\operatorname{EXTRACTION\_UNDEFINED}(s,a,D,h)\), \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t)\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}(D,b,\mathrm{retainedRows},t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t)\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t)\).

definitions.name: District-closed Layer-3 transport recursion
definitions.construction:
Initialize one finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_ho\wedge E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\); its denotation at \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) is \((P_{M^\star}(B_ho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\). The deterministic transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has these eight rules. \(\mathsf{NORM}\): replace the least \(\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\) by \(\operatorname{Normed}(	au,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\), where the total finite-state checker applies consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, and disjoint-normal-form rewriting and returns a derivation \(
u:P(e)=P(\operatorname{nf}(e))\); append \(\operatorname{NORM}(v,e,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\). \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\): for the least normalized node, enumerate its counterfactual ancestors \(H\), the assignments summed out, and a checked finite marginalization derivation \(\alpha\), then replace it by \(\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e|_H,\alpha)\) and append \(\operatorname{ANCESTOR}(v,H,\alpha)\). \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\): for the least ancestor-closed node, the compiler mechanically enumerates \(G[H]\), its districts, and all finite summation assignments and builds an acyclic sum-product DAG with leaves \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\); its checker constructs \(\sigma\) from finite marginalization and district-factorization rules, the DAG is spliced in, and \(\operatorname{SPLIT}(v,D_1,\ldots,D_k,\sigma)\) is appended. If enumeration or typing is undefined, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t))\). \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\): at the least \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\), enumerate all supplied \((s,a)\) canonically and retain a context and cell only when \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) succeeds and a checked proof gives \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\); the recomputed extraction tree must prove \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). Record every failed extraction and changed-district rejection without creating a row. Prepend the normalization row, stack accepted rows and values canonically as \((A_D,m_D)\), even if no non-normalization row survives, replace the node by \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A_D,m_D,Z_D(m_D),\kappa_{\mathrm{all}})\), and append the accepted rows, rejected candidates, admissibility proofs, and derivations; \(\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}\) checks \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\). \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\): for the least face node, compute \(Z=\{\omega:q(\omega)=0	ext{ for every }q\ge0	ext{ with }Aq=m\}\), with an exact LP or Farkas certificate for every coordinate, and test \(b\in\operatorname{row}(A)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\}\). If membership holds, fixed-pivot reduced row echelon form chooses \(b=\lambda^	op A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\); replace the node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\lambda^	op m,\delta_{\mathrm{face}})\), where the checker verifies \(bq=\lambda^	op Aq+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega q(\omega)=\lambda^	op m\), and append the certificates. If membership fails, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t))\); \(w_{\mathrm{local}}\) witnesses only variation in the district relaxation and is not a pair of globally compatible SCMs unless the one-district fiber-projection hypotheses have been checked. If no non-normalization extraction succeeded, use \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\) instead only after this normalization-only face test fails. \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\): replace the least ready \(\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\), all of whose children are resolved, by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\sum_{j\in J}F_j,\delta_{\mathrm{sum}})\), using finite additivity and child derivations. \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\): replace the least ready product node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\prod_jF_j,\delta_{\mathrm{prod}})\), using district factorization and child derivations. \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\): when both roots are \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_B,\delta_B)\) and \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_E,\delta_E)\), append a condition record and return \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) if the independent zero calculus proves \(F_E=0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\); return \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\) if the independent positivity calculus proves \(F_E>0\) throughout that fiber; return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t))\) if an explicitly checked \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) has \(F_E=0\); otherwise return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t))\). Rule priority is \(\mathsf{NORM}>\mathsf{ANCESTOR}>\mathsf{SPLIT}>\mathsf{EXTRACT}>\mathsf{FACE\_ID}>\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}>\mathsf{PRODUCT}>\mathsf{CONDITION}\); within a rule choose the least applicable node, where applicability includes readiness. No rule creates an earlier-phase node. For nonterminals, \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\): the rules respectively decrease the indicated first still-changeable coordinate, with \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) changing \(r_C=1\) to zero after the first seven coordinates vanish; later coordinates may increase. If no rule applies to a nonterminal, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t))\).

definitions.name: Cross-menu face-preservation handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{preserve}}\) starts from the exact feasible face \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) and tracks both its affine hull and forced-zero coordinates through ancestor restriction, fixing, district splitting, and marginalization in \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).

definitions.name: Layer-3 menu-acquisition handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{acquire}}\) enumerates realizable regime blocks \((R_e,p_e)\), propagates each full dependent block through the finite dual bases defining arm values on \(\mathcal K_S\), and solves the finite ex-post covering problem \(\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\) subject to \(\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).

definitions.name: Partial-district invariance-frontier handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{leak}}\) splits a selected district response kernel across \(D\cap\Delta_s\) and \(D\setminus\Delta_s\), tests whether supplied and target Layer-3 factors depend on a common invariant marginal kernel, and searches the smallest binary crossing perturbation when they do not.

definitions.name: Exact source-labelled global canonical polynomial fiber
definitions.construction:
For each \(s\in\mathcal S\), let \(\theta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\) range over \(\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\), the finite canonical SCM parameterization obtained by enumerating the structural tables compatible with \(G\) and the declared observed alphabets.  Its coordinates obey
\[
 p_{U}^{s}(u)\geq 0,\qquad \sum_{u\in\Omega_U}p_U^s(u)=1,
 \qquad
 \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^{s}\in\{0,1\},\qquad
 \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^{s}=1.
\]
The canonical exogenous variables are assigned to their graph-compatible district blocks, and blocks belonging to distinct districts have product law.  Thus the displayed constraints include recursive compatibility with \(G\) and district factorization, while retaining the original alphabet \(\mathcal X_V\) at every observed vertex.

For any finite counterfactual event \(C\) in domain \(s\), recursively evaluate the one-hot tables in topological order and define the cell polynomial
\[
 \Phi_C^s(\theta^s)
 =\sum_{u\in\prod_U\Omega_U}
   \mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under }(\mu^s,u)\}
   \prod_U p_U^s(u_U).
\]
The indicator is itself a finite polynomial in the one-hot coordinates by recursive substitution.  For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), let \(q_D^s(\omega_D;\theta^s)\) be the analogous polynomial obtained by summing the same monomials over the canonical exogenous assignments whose induced structural response profile on \(D\) is \(\omega_D\).

Writing \(C_{a,v}\) for the event that descriptor \(a\) returns \(v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\), define the exact global canonical fiber by
\[
\begin{split}
 \Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta=(\theta^s:s\in\mathcal S):{}&
 \theta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
 &q_D^s(\cdot;\theta^s)=q_D^\star(\cdot;\theta^\star)
   \quad\text{whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
 &\Phi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)
   \quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s,
   \ v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
All graph, one-hot, simplex, district-factorization, invariance, and complete supplied-law constraints are retained.  For a target-domain counterfactual cell \(T\), set
\[
 L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
 \qquad
 U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and for two arms with common evidence define
\[
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)
 =\Phi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
  -\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\), then for every available \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), \[K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^s.\] After, and only after, proving \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). The target arm numerator, evidence, and generic target cells equal \(n_{\rho,D}q_D^\star\), \(d_Dq_D^\star\), and \(b_Dq_D^\star\), respectively. Failed extraction yields no incidence row.
statements.justification: This converts every heterogeneous Layer-3 input and each target arm comparison into exact linear information on a fixed response carrier.
statements.gap: Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim give canonical response carriers, while CTFIDU+ extracts Layer-3 factors; neither gives a source-labelled common-evidence row system under district-level transport.
statements.consumer: The row representation supplies the primal and dual programs used by the face-aware identification and arm-ordering certificates.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), and a successful judgment
\(
 \operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa).
\)
By the canonical response-profile definition, \(q_D^s\) is a probability mass function on the finite set \(\Omega_D\).  For fixed \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), let \(C(h,c)\subseteq\Omega_D\) be the profiles which produce cell \(c\) at context \(h\) under regime \(a\).  By the incidence-row definition,
\[
 r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{\omega\in C(h,c)\}.
\]
The successful extraction certificate uses only consistency, unnesting, fixing at the declared context, and finite marginalization.  Typed-menu realizability therefore identifies its semantic kernel cell with the probability of \(C(h,c)\) under the response law of \(M^s\).  Consequently, by finite additivity,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)
 &=P_{M^s}\{\omega_D\in C(h,c)\} \\
 &=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_D}\mathbf 1\{\omega\in C(h,c)\}q_D^s(\omega) \\
 &=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^s.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Every quotient used to recover the displayed kernel is legitimate because success of the extraction judgment includes a nonzero certificate for that quotient; no equality is asserted on an unavailable or zero-denominator context.

If \(s=\star\), then \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\) by notation.  If instead \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives equality of the joint structural-response laws on \(D\), hence again \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\).  Thus, and only after one of these two admissibility facts has been checked,
\[
 K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star.
\]
Finally, the target-row definition applies exactly the same finite evaluation to \(B_\rho\cap E\), \(E\), and a generic reduced target cell.  It gives, respectively,
\[
 P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E)=n_{\rho,D}q_D^\star,
 \qquad P_{M^\star}(E)=d_Dq_D^\star,
 \qquad P_{M^\star}(\text{target cell})=b_Dq_D^\star.
\]
By the extraction and stacking definitions, a failed judgment has neither a certified kernel cell nor an incidence equality and therefore contributes no row to \(A_D\).

statements.statement: Suppose the union of variables visited by the reduced arm targets and every retained menu factor has one district \(D\), and \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). In particular, every point of the boundary face, not only its relative interior, is induced by a compatible SCM family on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\).
statements.justification: The equality is the causal realization step that makes optimization over the face sharp at the original observed cardinalities.
statements.gap: CTFIDU+ proves one-domain completeness by ctf-thickets and may enlarge observed alphabets; it does not identify a heterogeneous source-labelled compatibility fiber with a fixed-alphabet response polytope.
statements.consumer: Every primal optimizer or sign-reversing point returned by the later programs becomes an explicit compatible SCM rather than a formal probability vector.
statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathcal Q_D=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
We prove both inclusions.

First take \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  The normalization row of \(A_D\) gives \(\mathbf 1^\top q_D^\star=1\), and \(q_D^\star\geq0\) because it is a probability mass function.  For every other retained row, district-cell linearity and its checked source-admissibility proof give the corresponding equality
\(
 r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star=K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h).
\)
Stacking these equalities in the declared order yields
\[
 A_Dq_D^\star=m_D.
\]
Hence \(q_D^\star\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\), and therefore
\(
 \mathcal Q_D\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\)

For the reverse inclusion, nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) supplies a reference family \(\mathbf M_0\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Fix any \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  Because the reduced targets and every retained menu factor visit only the one district \(D\), a typed-menu cell in a target or transport-admissible source domain is, after consistency and unnesting, a finite disjoint union of fixed-context district cells.  No cross-district quotient is needed.  The successful extraction judgments therefore give all of those cell probabilities as incidence rows, and the equations \(A_Dq=m_D\) preserve their values cell by cell.  Finite additivity then preserves each supplied law in those domains.

We now realize \(q\) without changing any declared endogenous alphabet.  Introduce for district \(D\) a finite response variable \(U_D\) taking values in \(\Omega_D\) with
\[
 P(U_D=\omega)=q(\omega).
\]
At every parent configuration visited by a target or menu, the structural equation of each \(V\in D\) reads the component map \(f_V\) of \(U_D=\omega=(f_V:V\in D)\).  At an unvisited parent configuration, extend the map by the value used in \(\mathbf M_0\).  Acyclicity of \(G\) makes these equations recursive, and their outputs remain in the fixed set \(\mathcal X_V\).  Use this response block in the target domain and in every source domain satisfying \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  In a source domain satisfying \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\), retain the reference response block of \(\mathbf M_0\).  This dichotomy is exhaustive by district closure.  Retain all response blocks outside \(D\) from \(\mathbf M_0\), independently across districts.  Hence recursive compatibility and district factorization are preserved, and district-kernel invariance holds in every unchanged district.

In admissible domains the preceding cell calculation and \(A_Dq=m_D\) preserve every supplied menu law; in changed-
\(D\) domains the complete reference response block was retained, so their supplied laws are preserved as well.  Typed-menu realizability therefore gives a family \(\mathbf M_q\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and construction gives
\[
 q_D^\star(\mathbf M_q)=q.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\subseteq\mathcal Q_D\).  The construction permits zero masses in \(q\), so it realizes boundary points as well as relative-interior points on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

statements.statement: Suppose the union of variables visited by the reduced target and every retained menu factor has one district \(D\), and \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). A target row \(b_D\) is constant on \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) if and only if \[b_D\in\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}.\] If \(b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\), its value is \(\lambda^\top m_D\). If the membership fails, two SCM families on \(\mathcal X\) agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell.
statements.justification: Forced-zero coordinates repair the boundary-fiber failure of the ordinary global row-span criterion and yield an exact original-alphabet iff frontier.
statements.gap: Raghavan and Bareinboim give graphical completeness for Layer-3 inputs, but not this active-face characterization or a source-labelled fixed-cardinality separation theorem.
statements.consumer: A released menu that pins the response law to a simplex face can identify targets missed by ordinary row rank, without producing a false nullspace certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(K=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\), \(A=A_D\), \(m=m_D\), \(Z=Z_D(m_D)\), and let \(J=\Omega_D\setminus Z\).  The normalization row in \(A\) implies \(\mathbf 1^\top q=1\) for every \(q\in K\), so \(J\neq\varnothing\).  For each \(\omega\in J\), the definition of \(Z\) supplies \(q^{\omega}\in K\) with \(q^{\omega}(\omega)>0\).  The average
\[
 \bar q=\frac1{|J|}\sum_{\omega\in J}q^{\omega}
\]
belongs to \(K\), is zero on \(Z\), and is strictly positive on every coordinate in \(J\).

Define the feasible-direction space
\[
 L=\{v\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}:Av=0,\ v(\omega)=0\text{ for every }\omega\in Z\}.
\]
For any \(v\in L\), finiteness of \(J\) and strict positivity of \(\bar q\) on \(J\) allow a number \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\(
 \varepsilon |v(\omega)|\leq \bar q(\omega)/2
\)
for every \(\omega\in J\).  Then
\[
 \bar q+\varepsilon v\in K,
 \qquad \bar q-\varepsilon v\in K.
\]
It follows that the direction space of the affine hull of \(K\) is exactly \(L\): every difference of two points of \(K\) lies in \(L\), and the preceding two-sided perturbation realizes every direction in \(L\).

Let \(\widetilde A\) be obtained by appending the rows \(e_\omega\), \(\omega\in Z\), to \(A\).  Then \(L=\ker(\widetilde A)\).  Elementary finite-dimensional linear algebra gives
\[
 L^\perp=(\ker\widetilde A)^\perp
 =\operatorname{row}(\widetilde A)
 =\operatorname{row}(A)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\};
\]
indeed, row vectors annihilate the kernel, and equality follows because both sides have dimension \(\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde A)\).

By the one-district fiber-projection theorem and district-cell linearity, the target cell on a compatible family with response law \(q\) equals \(b_Dq\), and every \(q\in K\) occurs.  Thus the target is constant on \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) exactly when \(b_Dv=0\) for every \(v\in L\), which by the preceding display is exactly the claimed membership condition.  If
\[
 b_D=\lambda^\top A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega,
\]
then every \(q\in K\) satisfies
\[
 b_Dq=\lambda^\top Aq+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega q(\omega)
 =\lambda^\top m.
\]

If membership fails, choose \(v\in L\) with \(b_Dv\neq0\).  The two laws \(q_\pm=\bar q\pm\varepsilon v\) constructed above lie in \(K\) and satisfy
\[
 b_Dq_+-b_Dq_-=2\varepsilon b_Dv\neq0.
\]
The fiber-projection theorem supplies corresponding families \(\mathbf M_+,\mathbf M_-\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\).  They agree on every supplied law by membership in the same compatibility fiber and disagree on the target cell, which proves the asserted paired-model certificate.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), each nonterminal \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), or \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\) step preserves the ordered pair of root denotations pointwise. The preservation witnesses are respectively the checked normalization derivation, finite ancestor marginalization identity, checked district sum-product derivation, admissible extraction equations \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\), active-face calculation, finite additivity, and district factorization. The \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) rule labels its terminal with the same two root values and divides only under an independent strict-positivity certificate. In the rank \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\), the first seven rules respectively decrease \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi}\) while fixing every earlier coordinate, and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) decreases \(r_C\) after the others vanish; no rule creates an earlier-phase node. The fixed priority and least-applicable-node convention give a unique successor. From a well-typed initial configuration, \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable because every declared partial-operation failure takes its specified \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) branch.
statements.justification: A typed operational semantics needs a local invariant for every transition before terminal soundness follows.
statements.gap: The prior transport recursions prove their own rule systems sound, but do not cover certified Layer-3 extraction from heterogeneous source-labelled laws.
statements.consumer: The local invariant supports independent checking of a returned derivation or failure trace.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  We check the rules in their declared phase order.

For \(\mathsf{NORM}\), the attached derivation \(\nu\) is built from consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, Boolean normalization, and finite disjoint additivity.  Each constructor is an equality of events or of their probabilities, hence the replaced node and its successor have the same denotation.  For \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), the omitted finite variables are summed over their complete declared state spaces; therefore
\[
 P(e)=\sum_xP(e,x),
\]
which is the checked derivation \(\alpha\).  For \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), semi-Markovian district factorization applies to the enumerated districts of \(G[H]\); the finite sum over the enumerated assignments and product over district factors is exactly the original ancestor-closed probability.  These three substitutions therefore preserve every root that reaches the replaced node.

At \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), only a successful extraction with a proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) is retained.  District-cell linearity and district-kernel invariance give every retained equality, and stacking them with normalization gives
\[
 A_Dq_D^\star(\mathbf M)=m_D.
\]
The denotation of both \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,b)\) and its \(\operatorname{NeedFace}\) successor is, by the grammar, \(bq_D^\star(\mathbf M)\); rejected or failed candidates create no equation.  Thus extraction preserves denotation.

At \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), the checked representation
\(
 b=\lambda^\top A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega
\)
and the certified facts \(Aq_D^\star=m\) and \(q_D^\star(\omega)=0\) for \(\omega\in Z\) give
\[
 bq_D^\star=\lambda^\top m.
\]
Thus the resolved expression has the old face-node denotation.  For \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), finite additivity identifies the parent denotation with the sum of the resolved child denotations.  For \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\), district factorization identifies it with their product.  Hence each of the seven nonterminal transformation rules preserves both root denotations pointwise.

When both roots are resolved, \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) records those unchanged numerator and denominator values.  It constructs a quotient only when the separate certificate \(\pi\) proves strict positivity of the denominator throughout the compatibility fiber; its zero and failure branches perform no division.

It remains to check operational claims.  Each of the first seven rules decreases its designated coordinate of
\(
 \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)
\)
and fixes every earlier coordinate, while no rule creates an earlier-phase node.  Condition decreases \(r_C=1\) after the first seven coordinates vanish.  The canonical orders, fixed priority, and least-applicable-node convention select at most one successor.  Conversely, every well-typed nonterminal has a least unresolved phase.  The rule for that phase applies, and every failure of a partial operation is routed to its explicitly declared \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) constructor.  Therefore a well-typed run cannot reach \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).

statements.statement: For every realizable typed menu with \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), the priority transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has a unique finite run because \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}\in\mathbb N^8\) decreases lexicographically. Every reached configuration has root denotation \((P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If the result is \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\), then \(F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\), \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and \(F_B(\mathcal P)/F_E(\mathcal P)=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)\) for every compatible model. If \(z\) proves \(F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, the result is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) and the conditional is undefined. A split failure, failed extraction, normalization-only face failure, denominator witness at zero, or uncertified denominator positivity returns its typed \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) trace and performs no division. A \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\) witness certifies only local district-face variation and implies global nonidentification only when the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem are separately verified. The observed numerical sign of \(F_E\) is never itself a positivity certificate, and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.
statements.justification: The source-labelled Layer-3 recursion must be valid before its output can enter the sharper arm-ordering analysis.
statements.gap: CTFTR handles heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs and CTFIDU+ handles one-specification Layer-3 inputs; neither soundness argument covers both features simultaneously.
statements.consumer: A successful output can be evaluated directly from released source tables, while impossible conditioning events are rejected before division.
statements.proof_tex:
The initial two roots denote
\[
 \bigl(P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E),P_{M^\star}(E)\bigr)
\]
for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), by the recursion definition.  The transition-preservation lemma shows inductively over the run that every later configuration has the same ordered pair of root denotations.

The lexicographic order on \(\mathbb N^8\) is well founded: nested induction on the first coordinate, then the second, and so on, rules out an infinite sequence which decreases the first changed coordinate and fixes all earlier ones.  Every nonterminal transition strictly decreases this rank.  Hence the run is finite.  The fixed rule priority, canonical finite orders, and least-node convention give at most one successor, while the last paragraph of the transition lemma gives either a successor or a typed terminal.  Thus the finite run is unique and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable.

Suppose the terminal is
\(
 \operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi).
\)
The expression grammar is closed under the finite sums and products used by splitting and marginalization, and under certified quotients used by extraction and conditioning.  Starting from typed-menu cells and rational constants, induction over the two derivation trees therefore gives
\(
 F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P).
\)
Root preservation gives, for every compatible \(\mathbf M\),
\[
 F_B(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E),
 \qquad
 F_E(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(E).
\]
The independent certificate \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) on the whole fiber, so division is well typed and
\[
 \frac{F_B(\mathcal P)}{F_E(\mathcal P)}
 =\frac{P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E)}{P_{M^\star}(E)}
 =P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)
 =Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M).
\]

If the independent zero calculus instead supplies \(z:F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, then the evidence event has zero probability in every compatible model, so the conditional is undefined and the declared terminal is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\).  Each other listed failure is returned at the exact partial operation where its certificate is absent.  In particular, the numerical value of a denominator is not used as a proof of uniform positivity, and no failure branch divides.  Finally, a face-failure vector varies a district relaxation only.  The construction of two globally compatible SCMs requires the separate surjectivity conclusion of the one-district fiber-projection theorem; without its one-district hypotheses the recursion makes no global nonidentification claim.

statements.statement: Under the finite semi-Markovian convention, the observational and hard-interventional problem-instance subgrammar has a proper typed embedding \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\), and the one-domain problem-instance class has a proper typed embedding \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\) obtained by setting \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\). On either embedded class, every successful identifying functional returned by DCTFTR agrees semantically with the target query, and every successful functional returned by the published calculus agrees with that same query; no syntactic or transition-by-transition output equivalence is asserted. In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), CTFTR cannot accept the genuine cross-world cell \(p\), while the complete source-labelled family with \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\) is not realizable by one SCM and hence is not a single-specification CTFIDU+ instance.
statements.justification: Typed proper embeddings state exactly which published input classes are recovered and where the multi-domain Layer-3 language is strictly larger.
statements.gap: CTFTR and CTFIDU+ occupy different proper subgrammars; neither accepts the complete binary multi-domain instance.
statements.consumer: Users can recognize settled CTFTR and CTFIDU+ cases while reserving DCTFTR for genuinely heterogeneous Layer-3 inputs.
statements.proof_tex:
The DCTFTR typed-menu grammar permits observational, hard-interventional, and declared partial-copy descriptors.  Restricting each \(\mathcal A_s\) to its observational and hard-interventional constructors is therefore an injective type-preserving map from \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\) into \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\).  Likewise, imposing \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) removes source labels and selection changes but retains every one-specification Layer-3 descriptor, giving an injective type-preserving map from \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\).

For either embedding, recursion soundness proves that every successful DCTFTR expression equals the causal target in every compatible model.  The cited CTFTR and CTFIDU+ soundness results give the same semantic equality for a successful expression returned by the corresponding published calculus.  Equality to the same target is all that is claimed; the respective syntaxes and traces need not coincide.

Both embeddings are proper.  In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the supplied quantity
\[
 p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=\frac38
\]
is a joint cross-world cell, so it is not generated by the observational or hard-interventional descriptor constructors of CTFTR.  Thus the first embedding is not surjective.  For the second, a one-specification instance has one SCM law for the factual variable \(Z\).  The complete binary family instead requires simultaneously
\[
 P^\star(Z=1)=0,
 \qquad P^s(Z=1)=1.
\]
No single probability law can satisfy both equalities.  The family is a valid two-domain DCTFTR instance because \(Z\) is selected in the source domain, but it is not a one-specification CTFIDU+ instance.  Hence the second embedding is proper as well.

statements.statement: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.\] Consequently, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every compatible SCM if and only if the displayed dual has a certificate with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\), a primal minimizer induces an original-alphabet compatible SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\), primal minimizers and maximizers induce two original-alphabet compatible SCMs with opposite arm rankings.
statements.justification: The theorem replaces assumed sound intervals with an exact menu-weight certificate and an opposing SCM whenever the certificate has the opposite sign.
statements.gap: Park and Lee's CTF-POMIS is graph based and PATR supplies valid Layer-1/2 transported bounds; neither derives an iff dual certificate for arm order from heterogeneous Layer-3 cells on the compatibility face.
statements.consumer: A bandit analyst can audit a strict arm removal by checking one vector of source-table weights and can recover a concrete countermodel when the order reverses.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(K=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) and \(g=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\).  The normalization row of \(A_D\) gives \(\mathbf 1^\top q=1\) on \(K\).  Thus the assumed nonempty set \(K\) is a closed subset of the finite simplex and is compact.  The primal minimum and maximum are consequently attained.

Apply finite linear-programming strong duality to the primal variables \(q\), equality constraint \(A_Dq=m_D\), nonnegativity constraint \(q\geq0\), and cost column \(g^\top\).  Its dual variable \(\eta\) is unrestricted because the primal constraint is an equality, and the nonnegative primal variables give the coordinatewise constraint \(A_D^\top\eta\leq g^\top\).  Therefore
\[
 \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
 =\min_{q\in K}gq
 =\max_{\eta:A_D^\top\eta\leq g^\top}m_D^\top\eta.
\]
Weak duality is visible directly: for feasible \(q,\eta\),
\[
 m_D^\top\eta=q^\top A_D^\top\eta\leq gq.
\]

For every \(q\in K\), common positive evidence and the target-row identities give
\[
 Q_\sigma(q)-Q_\rho(q)
 =\frac{n_{\sigma,D}q-n_{\rho,D}q}{d_Dq}
 =\frac{gq}{d_Dq}.
\]
The denominator is strictly positive by hypothesis, so the sign of the conditional difference is the sign of \(gq\).  The one-district fiber-projection theorem says that these \(q\)'s are exactly the target district laws of compatible SCM families.  Hence every compatible SCM has \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) if and only if \(gq>0\) for every \(q\in K\).  Compactness makes this equivalent to \(\min_{q\in K}gq>0\), and dual attainment makes it equivalent to a feasible \(\eta\) with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\).

If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\), let \(q_-\) be a primal minimizer.  Fiber projection realizes \(q_-\) by an SCM family on \(\mathcal X\), and the displayed ratio has negative numerator, proving \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\).  If in addition \(\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)>0\), a maximizer \(q_+\) is likewise realized and has the opposite strict ranking.  Both families lie in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), so they agree on every supplied law and use the original observed alphabets.

statements.statement: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces are obtained from the feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of one closed interval, allowing zero, one, or two sign boundaries; each boundary returns both a dual menu-weight certificate on the pruning side and an original-alphabet SCM attaining equality.
statements.justification: This exposes the non-obvious phase boundary at which one extra Layer-3 cell changes an arm from possibly optimal to certifiably dominated.
statements.gap: The located identification papers treat a fixed menu, and the Park--Lee bandit papers prune from a fixed graph or fixed transported bounds; none gives a parametric Layer-3 menu-cell sign diagram with sharp boundary SCMs.
statements.consumer: A study designer can report exactly which realized partial-copy cell values would justify dropping an expensive or unsafe arm before online exploration.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(K=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\), \(r=r_D^\dagger\), and \(g=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\).  Since \(K\) is a nonempty compact convex polytope and \(q\mapsto rq\) is linear, its image
\[
 I_D=\{rq:q\in K\}
\]
is a nonempty compact convex subset of \(\mathbb R\), hence a closed interval.  Every \(p\in I_D\) has a nonempty compact fiber \(K(p)=\{q\in K:rq=p\}\), so the minimum defining \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is attained.

For \(p_0,p_1\in I_D\), choose minimizers \(q_0,q_1\).  If \(0\leq t\leq1\), then \(tq_0+(1-t)q_1\in K(tp_0+(1-t)p_1)\), and therefore
\[
 \Gamma(tp_0+(1-t)p_1;m_D)
 \leq t\Gamma(p_0;m_D)+(1-t)\Gamma(p_1;m_D).
\]
Thus the value function is convex.

The row-augmented primal has equality matrix \(\widetilde A=(A_D;r)\) and right side \((m_D;p)\).  Applying the primal--dual equality of the transported-dominance theorem to this augmented one-district face gives
\[
 \Gamma(p;m_D)
 =\max_{(\eta,\beta):A_D^\top\eta+\beta r^\top\leq g^\top}
 \{m_D^\top\eta+\beta p\}.
\]
The feasible polyhedron in \((\eta,\beta)\) is independent of \((m_D,p)\) and is described by finitely many rational inequalities.  Quotienting its lineality space, each relevant zero-dimensional feasible basis solves a nonsingular rational linear system, so its coordinates are rational.  There are finitely many such bases.  On any interval where one basis is optimal, the value is
\[
 m_D^\top\eta_B+\beta_Bp,
\]
whose slope is rational and whose intercept is a rational linear, hence rational affine, function of \(m_D\).  Taking the maximum of this finite list proves that the value function is finite, continuous, convex, and piecewise affine.  Degenerate bases merely repeat a piece and do not change the conclusion.

For a continuous convex function on an interval, the sublevel set
\[
 \{p\in I_D:\Gamma(p;m_D)\leq0\}
\]
is closed and convex, hence is empty, a point, or a closed interval.  Its relative complement is \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\), giving zero, one, or two transitions between nonpositive and strictly positive regimes.  At every such sign boundary \(p_0\), continuity gives \(\Gamma(p_0;m_D)=0\).  Dual attainment supplies \((\eta_0,\beta_0)\) with value zero there, and the same feasible dual basis supplies the displayed affine lower certificate on its adjacent pruning piece.  Primal attainment supplies \(q_0\in K(p_0)\) with \(gq_0=0\); one-district fiber projection realizes \(q_0\) by a compatible SCM on \(\mathcal X\).  Since \(d_Dq_0>0\), that SCM has equal conditional arm values, as claimed.

statements.statement: For \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the base face has the unique parameterization \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), and \[Q_\rho(q(p))=1-2p,\qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=1/2,\qquad I_D=[0,1/2],\qquad \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=2p-1/2,\qquad \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2].\] With the augmented row order consisting of the three rows of \(A_D\) followed by \(r_D^\dagger\), the dual vector \((0,-1,0,2)^\top\) represents \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) exactly and has value \(2p-1/2\); at the realized value \(p=3/8\) it certifies margin \(1/4\). The boundary SCM is \(q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), while \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal on the original binary alphabets. For the sole unit-cost block, \[\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\},\qquad \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.\] The first equality is witnessed by \(p=0\) for \(\rho\) and \(p=1/2\) for \(\sigma\); at \(p=3/8\), \(Q_\sigma=1/2>1/4=Q_\rho\), and no other arm exists because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\).
statements.justification: This exhaustive binary calculation verifies the sign frontier, the dual certificate, the boundary law, and the decision consequence in one complete instance.
statements.gap: The published identification and bandit papers do not exhibit a heterogeneous genuine Layer-3 cell whose observed value crosses an exact transported pruning boundary.
statements.consumer: The instance is a regression test for extraction, face identification, experiment blocking, and undefined-arm-safe pruning.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(q=(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4)^\top\) in the stated response-profile order.  The equations \(A_Dq=m_D\) are
\[
 q_1+q_2+q_3+q_4=1,
 \qquad q_3+q_4=\frac12,
 \qquad q_2+q_4=\frac12,
 \qquad q_j\geq0.
\]
Writing \(p=q_4\) gives
\[
 q_2=q_3=\frac12-p,
 \qquad q_1=p,
 \qquad 0\leq p\leq\frac12.
\]
This proves the unique parameterization \(q(p)\).  Since \(d_Dq(p)=1\), direct row multiplication yields
\[
 Q_\rho(q(p))=q_2+q_3=1-2p,
 \qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=q_2+q_4=\frac12,
\]
and the candidate row gives \(r_D^\dagger q(p)=q_4=p\), so \(I_D=[0,1/2]\).  Likewise,
\[
 \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q(p)
 =-q_3+q_4=2p-\frac12,
\]
whence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2]\).

In the augmented row order, multiplication gives
\[
 (0,-1,0,2)
 \begin{bmatrix}A_D\\ r_D^\dagger\end{bmatrix}
 =(0,0,-1,1)=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}.
\]
Thus this dual vector is feasible with equality and has objective
\[
 (0,-1,0,2)(1,1/2,1/2,p)^\top=2p-\frac12.
\]
At \(p=3/8\) it certifies the exact margin \(1/4\).  The three displayed laws
\[
 q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4),\quad
 q(0)=(0,1/2,1/2,0),\quad
 q(1/2)=(1/2,0,0,1/2)
\]
belong to the base face.  Their gap values are respectively \(0,-1/2,1/2\); the one-district projection theorem realizes all three on the original binary alphabets.

With no experiment, \(p=0\) makes \(\rho\) strictly better and \(p=1/2\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly better.  Therefore both arms are possibly optimal and
\(
 \operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\}.
\)
Acquiring the sole block imposes \(q_4=3/8\), and the parameterization shows
\[
 \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\}.
\]
At this point \(Q_\rho=1/4<1/2=Q_\sigma\).  Since the declared arm set contains no third arm,
\[
 \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}
 =\{\sigma\}.
\]

statements.statement: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\). If there exists \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) with \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0\), removing \(\rho\) cannot remove a maximizing arm from \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); an arm whose common evidence is certified zero is excluded as undefined rather than ranked.
statements.justification: This records the elementary decision consequence while keeping it out of the research kernel.
statements.gap: The exclusion rule itself is elementary and is not positioned as a strengthening of Park and Lee; the new content is the derived sharp certificate in Theorems 5 and 6.
statements.consumer: A counterfactual bandit can initialize exploration on the certificate-retained action set without treating undefined conditionals as low rewards.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume that the reduced arm comparison has the single district \(D\), as required by the proposed statement.  
Let \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  Feasibility of the stated dual vector and \(A_Dq=m_D\) give
\[
 g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q
 \geq q^\top A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}
 =m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0.
\]
Because \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(n_{\sigma,D}\) are incidence rows for subevents of the common evidence event, coordinatewise
\[
 0\leq n_{\rho,D}\leq d_D,
 \qquad 0\leq n_{\sigma,D}\leq d_D.
\]
In particular,
\[
 d_Dq\geq n_{\sigma,D}q
 =g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q+n_{\rho,D}q
 >0.
\]
Thus every compatible law has positive common evidence, and district-cell linearity gives
\[
 Q_\sigma(q)-Q_\rho(q)
 =\frac{g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q}{d_Dq}>0.
\]
Arm \(\rho\) is strictly dominated by the available comparator \(\sigma\) at every compatible law and therefore cannot be a maximizing arm.  Removing it cannot remove a maximizer.  If the independent zero calculus instead certifies that an arm's conditioning evidence has probability zero, recursion soundness says that its conditional value is undefined; excluding that arm is a domain-of-definition decision, not an ordering of an undefined quantity below a reward.

statements.statement:
The minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are computable for every finite instance by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and solving the finite linear feasibility problems that define \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\).  In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular.  In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district instance with two unit-cost Layer-3 cell experiments for which
\[
 \operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
 =\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Consequently the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns.  For this instance the exact acquisition problem reduces to
\[
 \min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
 \quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
whose unique solution is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\) with cost two.
The multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality is a matching dual lower-bound certificate for the continuous relaxation.
statements.proof_tex:
For the general computability claim, fix \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\).  The set \(\mathcal K_S\) is given by the finite equalities \(A_Dq=m_D\), \(R_eq=p_e\) for \(e\in S\), and inequalities \(q\geq0\).  For a candidate arm \(\rho\), common evidence reduces the comparison \(Q_\rho(q)\geq Q_\sigma(q)\), on \(d_Dq>0\), to the linear inequality
\[
 (n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})q\geq0.
\]
Positive evidence is checked by maximizing \(d_Dq\) subject to \(q\in\mathcal K_S\) and all of these arm-comparison inequalities, and requiring a positive optimum.  Thus membership of \(\rho\) in \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\) is decided by one finite linear program.  There are only \(2^{|\mathcal U|}\) sets \(S\), so enumerating them, retaining those with \(\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), and minimizing \(\sum_{e\in S}c_e\) returns all minimum-cost solutions.

We construct the obstruction on the binary graph \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\), with the singleton district \(D=\{Y\}\), sure evidence, and response order
\(
 \Omega_D=((0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)).
\)
Take the base face to be the whole simplex.  Let \(\rho\) be treatment zero and \(\sigma\) treatment one with reward \(Y=1\); hence
\[
 n_{\rho,D}=(0,0,1,1),
 \qquad n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1),
 \qquad g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,1,-1,0).
\]
Use the realizable target response law
\[
 q^\star=(1/4,3/8,1/8,1/4).
\]
Experiment \(e_1\) reveals the genuine Layer-3 cell
\(
 q_2=P(Y_0=0,Y_1=1)=3/8
\), and \(e_2\) reveals
\(
 q_3=P(Y_0=1,Y_1=0)=1/8
\); each has unit cost.  These are zero-one incidence rows and are realized by the displayed finite response law, so the typed blocks are admissible.

With no experiment, laws with \(q_2-q_3<0\) and with \(q_2-q_3>0\) both occur.  Under \(e_1\) alone, the feasible choices \((q_2,q_3)=(3/8,5/8)\) and \((3/8,0)\), with the remaining mass zero or assigned to a zero-gap coordinate, give opposite strict rankings.  Under \(e_2\) alone, the choices \((q_2,q_3)=(0,1/8)\) and \((7/8,1/8)\) likewise give opposite rankings.  Hence both arms are possibly optimal in the first three faces.  When both blocks are acquired, every feasible law satisfies
\[
 g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q=q_2-q_3=\frac38-\frac18=\frac14>0,
\]
so only \(\sigma\) is possibly optimal.  The one-district projection construction realizes every displayed witness on the original binary alphabets.

Therefore
\[
 f(\{e_2\})-f(\varnothing)=0
 <1=f(\{e_1,e_2\})-f(\{e_1\}),
\]
which refutes submodularity with \(S=\varnothing\), \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), and \(e=e_2\).  Finally, matching the full-information set requires both equalities: omitting either one leaves both arms possibly optimal by the witnesses above.  With binary acquisition variables this is exactly \(x_1+x_2\geq2\); enumeration of its four integer points certifies the unique optimum \((1,1)\) and objective two.
For the continuous relaxation, the dual of \(\min x_1+x_2\) subject to \(x_1+x_2\geq2\) and \(x_i\geq0\) is
\[
 \max_{0\leq y\leq1}2y.
\]
The dual multiplier \(y=1\) gives the lower bound two, matched by the integer point \((1,1)\).  This is an exact mixed-integer optimality certificate, not merely an exhaustive numerical claim.

statements.statement: Under the frozen transport assumptions, district closure has no nontrivial strictly weaker graph-only replacement for a partially selected district.  More precisely, omit district closure while retaining district-kernel invariance exactly as stated, and let \(0<|D\cap\Delta_s|<|D|\).  Then every nonconstant binary incidence row on \(\Omega_D\) admits two finite original-alphabet SCM families having identical supplied source laws but different target values of that row.  Hence, based on a source row alone, the universally transportable rows are exactly the constant rows.  If one additionally assumes invariance of the marginal response law on \(I=D\setminus\Delta_s\), then a row transports for every compatible pair if and only if it is constant on every fiber of the coordinate projection \(\Omega_D\to\Omega_I\); this condition is decidable by finite enumeration, and failure gives a two-point leakage certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Retain district-kernel invariance with its frozen antecedent.  When
\(
 0<|D\cap\Delta_s|<|D|
\), that antecedent \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) is false, so the assumption imposes no equality at all between \(q_D^s\) and \(q_D^\star\).  This is the obstruction: the graph and the partial selection set alone do not specify any invariant within-district response marginal.

Let \(r\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\) be nonconstant.  Choose \(\omega_0,\omega_1\in\Omega_D\) with \(r(\omega_0)=0\) and \(r(\omega_1)=1\).  Construct two source-labelled families as follows.  In both families use the same source response law \(q_D^s=\delta_{\omega_0}\), so every supplied source law, including the cell \(rq_D^s=0\), is identical.  Use no informative target menu row beyond normalization.  In the first family take \(q_D^\star=\delta_{\omega_0}\); in the second take \(q_D^\star=\delta_{\omega_1}\).  Extend each deterministic profile at unvisited parent configurations by any fixed value in the declared nonempty alphabet, and retain identical deterministic response blocks in every other district and domain.  These are finite recursive SCMs on \(\mathcal X\), district factorization holds because the other district blocks are fixed independently, and the unchanged frozen kernel-invariance conditions hold in every wholly unselected district.  On the partially selected district they impose no restriction.  The two target values are
\[
 r\delta_{\omega_0}=0,
 \qquad r\delta_{\omega_1}=1.
\]
Thus every nonconstant source row has an original-alphabet paired-SCM leakage witness.  A constant row plainly has the same expectation under all probability laws, proving the asserted exact characterization under the frozen assumptions with closure removed.

For completeness, suppose a genuinely new marginal-kernel premise is stated explicitly:
\[
 (\mathrm{KMI})\qquad (\pi_I)_\#q_D^s=(\pi_I)_\#q_D^\star,
 \qquad I=D\setminus\Delta_s,
\]
where \(\pi_I\) restricts a district response profile to the response maps on \(I\).  If \(r=\widetilde r\circ\pi_I\), then
\[
 rq_D^s
 =\sum_{u\in\Omega_I}\widetilde r(u)(\pi_I)_\#q_D^s(u)
 =\sum_{u\in\Omega_I}\widetilde r(u)(\pi_I)_\#q_D^\star(u)
 =rq_D^\star,
\]
so the row transports.  Conversely, if \(r\) is not constant on a fiber, choose \(\omega_0,\omega_1\) in that fiber with different row values.  The laws \(\delta_{\omega_0}\) and \(\delta_{\omega_1}\) have the same \(\pi_I\)-marginal but different \(r\)-expectations, giving a two-point leakage certificate.  Testing all pairs of profiles with equal \(\pi_I\) is finite.  This proves both necessity and sufficiency under \((\mathrm{KMI})\), while also showing why \((\mathrm{KMI})\), which is absent from the frozen core, cannot be inferred from the graph alone.

statements.statement:
Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\).  The set \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set of finite dimension, and canonical realization on the declared observed alphabets gives, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
 \bigl\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):
       \mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
 =
 \bigl\{(\Phi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
       \theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\bigr\}.
\]
Consequently, the extrema \(L_T(\mathcal P)\) and \(U_T(\mathcal P)\) are attained and are the sharp bounds for every target cell \(T\).  The bounds are strictly tighter than the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when \(L_T(\mathcal P)>0\) or \(U_T(\mathcal P)<1\), an exactly checkable property of the displayed program.  The cell is identified if and only if \(L_T(\mathcal P)=U_T(\mathcal P)\); if \(L_T(\mathcal P)<U_T(\mathcal P)\), minimizing and maximizing canonical parameters yield two SCM families on the original observed alphabets that agree on every cell of every complete supplied law and disagree on \(T\).

Let
\[
 e_-=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star),
 \qquad
 e_+=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star).
\]
If \(e_+ =0\), the evidence has probability zero throughout the compatibility fiber; if \(e_-=0<e_+\), its positivity is not uniform.  In both cases a conditional functional on the entire fiber is rejected before division.  If \(e_->0\), the sharp range of the conditional arm value is
\[
 \left[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)},
 \quad
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)}
 \right],
\]
with both endpoints attained.  Under the same condition \(e_->0\), uniform strict ordering satisfies
\[
 \begin{array}{rcl}
 Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)>0,\\[3pt]
 Q_\rho^\star>Q_\sigma^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0,
 \end{array}
\]
and two original-alphabet compatible families with opposite strict rankings exist if and only if
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0
